newsitem.title: UK: Ethiopian airliner insured for $40 million - market.
newsitem.headline: Ethiopian airliner insured for $40 million - market.

text.p: A hijacked Ethiopian Airlines Boeing 767-200 airliner which crashed on Saturday off the Comoro Islands in the Indian Ocean was insured for $40 million, London based insurance sources told Reuters.

Primary insurer was the Ethiopian Insurance Corporation, but the risk was widely reinsured and was led by a Lloyd's of London syndicate, said a spokesman for broker Nicholson Leslie, a part of Aon Corp, which placed the risk.

The airline retained only a small part of the risk itself and had substantial liability insurance "to industry standards", insurers said. Liability cover, which is separate from hull insurance, will be provided under all-risks insurance.
The aircraft, which was built in 1987, is expected to be declared a war loss, market sources said. Some 30 to 40 Lloyd's of London syndicates provide hull war insurance.
There were 175 passengers and crew on board the plane, which was hijacked on Saturday, en route to Nairobi and west Africa from Addis Ababa, and crashed into the sea after running out of fuel.
Fifty-two people survived. The rest are dead or presumed dead. Police said around 40 bodies had still to be recovered from the wreckage.
